---
title: Formatting
---

`biblint format` writes a canonical representation of the structured BibTeX it understands.
The default profile is intentionally small: it normalizes layout, entry-type spelling, and field-name spelling without deciding how values or records should be rewritten.

## Default shape

Input:

```bibtex
@ARTICLE{Smith2024,
author={Smith, John},
title={A Study},
year=2024
}
```

Default output:

```bibtex
@article{Smith2024,
  author = {Smith, John},
  title = {A Study},
  year = 2024
}
```

The default does not align equals signs, insert blank lines, sort entries or fields, add braces, change numeric/month values, or clean up duplicate and empty fields.

## Layout and ordering

```toml
[format]
indent = 2                 # a space count, or "tab"
align = false              # or a field-name column number
blank-lines = true
trailing-commas = true
wrap = 80                  # false disables wrapping
sort = ["key"]
sort-fields = ["title", "author", "year"]
```

`align = false` is the explicit no-alignment setting.
`sort = true` uses the key order, and `sort-fields = true` uses biblint's built-in field order; lists provide an explicit order.

## Value transforms

These settings are opt-in because they alter value spelling or representation:

| Setting     | Effect                                                     |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `curly`         | Enclose values in braces.                                  |
| `numeric`         | Render numeric values as bare literals.                    |
| `months`         | Normalize recognized month names.                          |
| `format-page-ranges`        | Normalize page ranges.                                     |
| `escape` / `unescape` | Convert supported text between Unicode and LaTeX forms.    |
| `encode-urls`        | Encode URL underscores.                                    |
| `strip-enclosing-braces`        | Remove one outer brace group.                              |
| `enclosing-braces` / `remove-braces` | Select fields whose brace depth should change.             |
| `drop-all-caps`        | Convert all-caps textual values to title case.             |
| `wrap`        | Wrap long textual values at a configured width.            |
| `lowercase`        | Lowercase entry types and field names. Enabled by default. |

The escape table is deliberately package-independent.
Characters it cannot convert are preserved and can be reported by the `unsupported_escape` rule.

## Cleanup and semantic transforms

```toml
[format]
remove-empty-fields = true
remove-duplicate-fields = true
omit = ["abstract"]
strip-comments = true
tidy-comments = true
max-authors = 3
generate-keys = true
duplicate-kinds = ["doi", "citation"]
merge = "combine"
```

Cleanup and identity-changing settings can remove information, change author lists, generate keys, or merge entries.
`merge` accepts `first`, `last`, `combine`, and `overwrite`.
When no `duplicate-kinds` are supplied, merge considers DOI, citation, and abstract duplicates; key duplicates are included only when `key` is listed explicitly.

`generate-keys` uses the same formula evaluator as the `key_format` rule.
See [Citekey generation](key-generation.md) for its independent Better BibTeX syntax subset.

## Fix safety

`check --fix` applies safe formatting edits by default.
If the active format configuration includes a transform that can change content or identity, the formatting edit is marked unsafe and requires:

```console
biblint check references.bib --fix --unsafe-fixes
```

The standalone `format` command applies the configured format profile directly.
This distinction makes the check workflow suitable for automated post-edit passes while leaving intentional semantic changes visible in configuration and review.

## Preserved source

Comments, special entries, and unstructured source are retained unless a configured transform targets them.
If the parser cannot represent a construct, biblint preserves it and reports `unsupported_construct`; it does not discard unknown source to make the output appear clean.
